evidence_items.explanation: Across eight reasoning models and twelve tasks, the study reports price reversals in 32% of model-pair comparisons and attributes differences to reasoning tokens and interaction turns. This supports the proposed mechanism, but the comparisons are between models rather than a representative time series.

evidence_items.locator: Section 5, Inference Prices for Frontier Models Are Increasing Rapidly; also Sections 2.1 and 2.3
evidence_items.explanation: Using April 2024–November 2025 prices and benchmark token consumption, the paper finds rising costs for the best-performing models but falling costs at fixed performance. This supports a narrower frontier-cost claim and cautions against extending it to comparable useful output generally.
